name: Butter Chicken Pasta

ingredients.buy: 2 lb 5 oz dry short pasta (penne, rigatoni or rotini)

writer_notes: All 20 locked ingredient lines are used by a step; no orphans and no step uses an unbought item.
Only locked-view numbers appear in prose: 630 cal, 40.2 g protein, 14 servings. Cost shown only as the {{cost_ps}} token plus the standard $1/month membership line.
No cost_lines were provided in this dispatch, so shop_smart makes zero package-cost or per-ounce or lasts-N-batches claims; bullets cover form, substitution, and where-to-find only.
Source and locked view agree on a clean 3.5x scale from the origin recipe (1 lb chicken to 3.5 lb, 300 g pasta to ~1050 g, 1 tsp spices to 3.5 tsp).

prose.intro_html:
Butter chicken and a bowl of pasta walked into the same pan, and honestly, they should have done it years ago. This is the creamy, spiced, tomato-warmed sauce you love off a plate of naan, wrapped around short pasta so it holds a whole week of lunches without asking for a side of rice. The chicken breast keeps it lean and serious, the garam masala keeps it interesting, and a spoon of almond butter does the quiet work of making the sauce taste richer than it has any right to.

Here is the part I like. One batch lands at 630 calories and 40.2 grams of protein per serving, with 72.9 grams of carbs to actually fuel your afternoon. That is a real dinner doing a real job, not a sad container of plain grilled chicken. Cook it once, portion fourteen, and let future you thank present you every single day.
prose.shop_smart:
• Any short pasta with ridges or tubes works here. Penne, rigatoni, or rotini all grab the sauce well, so buy whatever shape is on the shelf and skip the fancy imported box.
  • Boneless skinless chicken breast is the anchor. Buy a family pack and cut it into bite-sized pieces yourself instead of paying someone to pre-cube it for you.
  • Garam masala, cumin, coriander, chili powder, and turmeric are the whole personality of this dish. If you are building a spice drawer, the store-brand jars taste the same as the pretty ones and this recipe uses them all, so nothing sits unopened.
  • Tomato sauce here means plain passata, smooth strained tomatoes with no added onion or herbs. Read the can so you are not buying seasoned marinara by accident.
  • Almond butter is the secret handshake. Plain unsweetened is what you want, not the honey-roasted snacking kind. A little jar covers this and leaves you plenty for toast.
  • Half and half brings the creaminess. Fresh ginger and a bunch of cilantro round it out, and both keep in the fridge long enough to earn their spot.
prose.make_it:
Start the pasta first so it is ready when the sauce is. Cook your short pasta to al dente right by the package directions, and before you drain it, scoop out a cup or two of that starchy pasta water and set it aside. That water is your thickness dial later, so do not pour it all down the sink.

Heat the olive oil and butter together in a large pan over medium heat. Add the chicken and let it cook until it is golden on all sides. Stir in the onion, garlic, and ginger and keep it moving for two to three minutes until everything softens and smells like dinner.

Now the spices. Add the garam masala, cumin, coriander, chili powder, turmeric, and red pepper flakes, and cook for one minute stirring constantly so they bloom instead of scorch. Stir in the tomato paste and the tomato sauce and combine, adding a splash of that reserved pasta water if it looks too thick.

Stir in the almond butter until it melts into the sauce, then pour in the half and half. Bring it to a boil, then drop the heat and simmer four to five minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the back of a spoon. Add the cooked pasta to the pan and toss until every piece is dressed in sauce. Finish with freshly chopped cilantro, season with salt and pepper to taste, and it is done.
prose.portion_html:
Here is the honest way to split fourteen even containers: weigh the pot. Set your empty pan on the scale before you start or note its weight, then weigh the whole finished dish, subtract the pot, and divide what is left by fourteen. That target number per container beats eyeballing every time, because the person who eats the last one deserves the same dinner as the person who eats the first.

Scoop to that weight, top each with a little of the reserved cilantro, and let them cool before the lids go on. Fourteen containers, each landing at 630 calories and 40.2 grams of protein, ready to grab on the way out the door.
prose.cost_closing_html:
When the pan is empty and the fridge is full, this whole thing comes out to {{cost_ps}} per serving. Fourteen dinners of spiced, creamy butter chicken pasta for the price most places charge you for one, and yours has the protein numbers to prove it is doing something.

That is the entire Thrifty Crew idea in one pan. Cook with intention, portion with a scale, and eat well without watching your grocery budget catch fire.

head.description: Creamy butter chicken pasta made for meal prep, with lean chicken breast, warm garam masala, and a spiced tomato cream sauce. 630 calories and 40.2 g protein per serving, scaled to 14 containers.

steps: Cook the short pasta to al dente per the package directions. Reserve one to two cups of pasta water, then drain.
Heat the olive oil and butter in a large pan over medium heat. Add the chicken and cook until golden on all sides.
Stir in the onion, garlic, and ginger and cook for two to three minutes until softened.
Add the garam masala, cumin, coriander, chili powder, turmeric, and red pepper flakes. Cook one minute, stirring constantly.
Add the tomato paste and tomato sauce and stir to combine, loosening with a bit of reserved pasta water if it is too thick.
Stir in the almond butter, then add the half and half. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, and simmer four to five minutes until thickened.
Add the cooked pasta to the pan and toss to coat well in the sauce.
Stir in chopped cilantro, season with salt and pepper to taste, and portion into containers.
